correctness.rationale: For all n>=1, FIFO order proves the Dyck/permutation encoding. A primitive nonmountain excursion produces interlacement induced P3 and unequal two-paths, whose interchange preserves every oriented bigram and singleton count. Mountain blocks have unique Euler traversal by forced bridges and uniquely forced cycles, giving global singleton against unrestricted competitors. Each ordered composition/permutation pair contributes exactly one source. Independent arborescence/BEST and brute-force checks agree for all nonnesting n<=6, unrestricted sources n<=5; an independent switch checker agrees on Dyck paths n<=9. Finite tests support but do not prove the all-length theorem.

value.rationale: The natural FIFO/Catalan language is not all globally reconstructible under 2-gram counts, unlike noncrossing words. The theorem gives a necessary-and-sufficient structural certificate, a constructive ambiguity operation, and the exact exponentially small globally rigid fraction, explaining a qualitative change between two equinumerous natural language families. The numerical sequence itself was known and is explicitly not presented as new.
